record.paper_title: On Global Hyperbolicity of Spacetimes: Topology Meets Functional Analysis
record.context_brief: Compact intervals versus bicontinuity in posets
record.original_question: Let (A, ≺) be a partially ordered set equipped with its interval topology. Suppose every closed interval [a,b] = {x : a ⪯ x ⪯ b} is compact in that topology. Must (A, ≺) then be bicontinuous in the domain-theoretic sense, meaning that the way-below relation is characterized both by directed suprema and dually by filtered infima, with each upper set ↑x filtered and having infimum x? More broadly, is there an order-theoretic analogue of the spacetime result that compact causal diamonds imply causality in non-compact spacetimes of dimension greater than 2, and if so what should play the role of the dimensional hypothesis for posets, or does no such restriction arise in the purely order-theoretic setting?

evidence.quote: Question 1: Consider a globally hyperbolic poset (A, ≺). Does the compactness of the intervals [a, b], under the interval topology, imply the bicontinuity of (A, ≺), in a similar fashion that the compactness in the closed diamonds in a spacetime M, under the Alexandrov topology TA, implies the (strong) causality of M (for dimensions strictly greater than 2)?

The only problem, towards [16], of considering a globally hyperbolic poset, is that we are left only with an order-theoretic structure; what would be, if there is such, the equivalent condition in [16] of “dimension strictly greater than 2”? Is there a possibility that the condition on the dimension applies only to globally hyperbolic spacetimes, while the proposed conjecture holds in globally hyperbolic posets without any restriction?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(A,\preceq)$ be a partially ordered set. For $a,b\in A$, write $[a,b]=\{x\in A:a\preceq x\preceq b\}$. Equip $A$ with the interval topology, i.e.\ the topology generated by the subbasis of sets of the form $\{x: x\not\preceq a\}$ and $\{x: a\not\preceq x\}$ for $a\in A$ (equivalently, having as a subbasis of closed sets the principal up-sets ${\uparrow}a=\{x:a\preceq x\}$ and the principal down-sets ${\downarrow}a=\{x:x\preceq a\}$).

Recall the way-below relation $\ll$ on a poset: $x\ll y$ iff for every directed set $D\subseteq A$ with a supremum $\sup D$, the inequality $y\preceq \sup D$ implies $x\preceq d$ for some $d\in D$. Dually, $x\ll^{op} y$ iff for every filtered set $F\subseteq A$ with an infimum $\inf F$, $\inf F\preceq x$ implies $f\preceq y$ for some $f\in F$. The poset $(A,\preceq)$ is called bicontinuous if:

(i) for every $x\in A$, the set ${\downarrow\!\!\ll}\,x=\{a:a\ll x\}$ is directed with supremum $x$;
(ii) for every $x\in A$, the set ${\uparrow\!\!\ll}\,x=\{a:x\ll a\}$ is filtered with infimum $x$;
(iii) $a\ll b$ if and only if $a\ll^{op} b$.

Question: Suppose that every closed interval $[a,b]$ is compact in the interval topology of $(A,\preceq)$. Must $(A,\preceq)$ be bicontinuous in the above sense? 

If additionally an order-theoretic analogue is required of the result that, for spacetimes of dimension strictly greater than $2$, compactness of all causal diamonds implies (strong) causality, identify what (if any) hypothesis on $(A,\preceq)$ should replace the dimension condition; in particular, does the implication "compact intervals $\Rightarrow$ bicontinuity" hold for all posets without any such restriction?
artifact.status_search_result: A search did not surface a published resolution of this specific implication "compact intervals in the interval topology $\Rightarrow$ bicontinuity" for arbitrary posets, nor an order-theoretic analogue of the dimension-$>2$ hypothesis used in the spacetime setting. The Martin–Panangaden framework establishes the converse direction (bicontinuity plus compact intervals characterizes globally hyperbolic posets, equivalent to interval domains), but the question of whether compactness of intervals alone forces bicontinuity appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Globally Hyperbolic Spacetimes as Posets
status_evidence.snippet: A poset (X,≤) is globally hyperbolic if it is bicontinuous and each interval [a,b] is compact in the interval topology.
status_evidence.claim: The standard definition couples bicontinuity with compact intervals; the implication from compact intervals alone to bicontinuity is not asserted.

status_evidence.title: A Domain of Spacetime Intervals in General Relativity
status_evidence.snippet: If a spacetime M is globally hyperbolic, then (M,⊑) is a bicontinuous poset with ≪=I⁺ whose interval topology is the manifold topology.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the spacetime-to-poset direction but does not resolve whether compactness of intervals in a general poset forces bicontinuity.
